text:
Dodgers adjust lineup as Teoscar Hernandez moves down amid cold streak
LAX Leader
The Los Angeles Dodgers set their lineup against the Atlanta Braves as they aim to even the series on Aug. 26. The team lost 4-3 on Tuesday, unable to complete a late comeback after Shohei Ohtani led off the ninth inning with a triple. Tyler Glasnow made his first start since returning from injury, delivering a solid performance following a difficult first inning, but did not receive sufficient run support.
Roki Sasaki is scheduled to pitch for the Dodgers on Wednesday. Sasaki has posted a 4.42 earned run average this season with 114 strikeouts over 116 innings. Since the All-Star break, he has improved significantly, recording a 2.31 earned run average and striking out 34 batters in 35 innings while allowing only two home runs compared to nineteen in the first half of the season.
The Dodgers’ batting order remains similar to Tuesday’s game, with Shohei Ohtani as designated hitter leading off, followed by Freddie Freeman at first base and Mookie Betts at shortstop occupying the top three spots in the lineup. Max Muncy continues in the cleanup position at third base, while Tommy Edman plays second base and follows him in the batting order.
Kyle Tucker will play right field and bat sixth; Alek Thomas moves up to seventh spot playing center field; Teoscar Hernandez shifts down to eighth position in left field for Wednesday’s game; Hunter Feduccia rounds out the lineup as catcher.
For Atlanta, right-hander AJ Smith-Shawver will start on Wednesday. Smith-Shawver holds a 6.23 earned run average through two starts this season, having allowed six earned runs over eight and two-thirds innings pitched with seven strikeouts.
The Dodgers’ offense managed several strong innings during Tuesday’s contest and will seek similar results against Smith-Shawver when Wednesday's game begins at 4:15 p.m.
